title: Rally writes report why they failed
outcome: A failed rally submission surfaces the error it actually got. The three write actions that still call fetch directly move onto the shared HTTP client, so failures arrive as a typed error carrying status and code instead of a bare Error, and a hung request eventually settles instead of waiting forever.
acceptanceCriteria: The rally create, rally update and substitution create actions go through the shared HTTP client; no write action calls fetch directly.
A 5xx rally submission renders the server-error toast and a 4xx renders its own message, which today never happens because the generic thrown Error never matches the branching.
The substitution create action rethrows on failure instead of swallowing the error and returning undefined.
The shared client accepts a timeout and rejects with a recognisable error when it elapses, using the platform's own AbortSignal rather than a new dependency.
A network-layer failure is normalised into the same error type as an HTTP failure, so a caller can tell disconnection from a rejected request without inspecting a TypeError.
